name: Intuit
key_signal: Forward P/E has collapsed to just 10.6x (from a historic premium multiple) even though revenue and earnings are still growing ~10% with 47% operating margins, while price has stabilized with a positive MACD histogram and +4% 21-day momentum after a brutal 48% six-month drawdown.
thesis: Intuit's stock has been cut roughly in half from its 52-week high ($813.7 to $291), pricing in what looks like a severe de-rating of a business that is still growing revenue at 10.4% and earnings at 10.7%, with 80.8% gross margins, 47% operating margins, and 22.5% ROE. At a forward P/E of just 10.6x for a company with these margins and a moderate debt-to-equity of 33.4, the valuation now implies either a permanent structural impairment to the TurboTax/QuickBooks franchise or a significant overreaction. The technical picture, while still below both the 50- and 200-day moving averages, shows tentative stabilization: RSI is neutral at 52.7, MACD histogram is positive (+5.7), and 21-day momentum has turned positive (+4.1%) even as longer-term momentum remains deeply negative. Sell-side consensus is still 'buy' across 33 analysts, and free cash flow of $5.2B against a $79.6B market cap (a ~6.6% FCF yield) provides a fundamental floor if the AI-disruption narrative proves overblown.
bear_case: The magnitude of this drawdown (-48% over six months, -64% from 52-week high, price still 40% below its 200-day SMA of $481, no golden cross) is not typical multiple compression — it signals the market has structurally repriced Intuit's moat, likely on fears that generative AI will commoditize tax prep and bookkeeping, disintermediating TurboTax and QuickBooks pricing power; if that thesis is correct, the currently 'strong' 10.4% revenue growth and 47% operating margins are trailing/lagging indicators that will decay going forward, and the stock's cheap forward P/E is a value trap rather than an opportunity, with 44.8% annualized volatility signaling the market still sees this as a high-uncertainty situation, not a bottom.
